# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schemas/tour-author.schema.json

format: storytilecraft-tour/1

id: collab.drawing
slug: collab-drawing
version: 1
status: published

title: Drawing together
description: How a shared canvas works when someone else is drawing with you.
category: collaboration
estimatedMinutes: 3

requirements:
  targets: [button.collab]

  unavailableHint: |
    Drawing together is switched off in this browser. Open {icon:gear} Settings → Collab Drawing and turn on **Enable Collab Drawing**, then come back — {icon:collab} will appear at the top right, and nothing here is missing from the app itself.

launch:
  sources: [editor, deep-link]
  autoStart: never
  resume: true
  restart: ask

session:
  content: user
  onEnd: keep

setup:
  - command: ui.setupLocation
    args:
      location: canvas
    onFailure: skip-action

defaults:
  interactionMode: NONE
  advance: manual
  targetPadding: 8

steps:
  - id: intro
    kind: info

    title: Drawing together
    body: |
      When you share a room, you and the other person draw on the same story. Everything either of you adds shows up on both screens. This tour walks through it once, at your pace.

  - id: who-is-here
    kind: interaction

    title: Who's in the room
    body: |
      Tap the collaboration button to open the panel.

      It lists everyone here, and the crown marks whoever opened the room. It closes whenever you tap the canvas — that's normal, and this button brings it back.

    target: button.collab
    panel:
      anchor: { target: button.collab, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      state: target.resolvable
      args:
        target: panel.collab
      operator: truthy

    fallback:
      type: show-info
      content:
        title: Collaboration isn't set up here
        body: |
          This tour needs a shared room. Open one from the start screen, then come back to it.

  - id: wait-peer
    kind: transition

    title: Waiting for someone to join
    body: |
      Share your room link or code, and this step continues by itself as soon as they arrive. Nothing is lost while you wait.

    waitFor:
      state: collab.participantCount
      operator: gte
      value: 2

    timeoutMs: 120000

    fallback:
      type: show-info
      content:
        title: Still on your own
        body: |
          Nobody joined yet. You can keep going through the tour and invite someone later — the room stays open.

  - id: same-story
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} Same story, both screens"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} to line your panels up in a row. Ask the other person to tap it too: each screen decides where its own panels sit, so running it on both is what lines your stories up.

    target: frames_to_strip_exposition
    panel:
      anchor: { target: frames_to_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: frames_to_strip_exposition

    fallback: skip-step

  - id: your-turn
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} Draw something"
    body: |
      Draw a stroke inside this first panel. The other person sees it appear on their screen as soon as you lift your finger.

    target:
      id: canvas.frame
      args:
        index: 0
      padding: 6
    panel:
      anchor: { target: canvas.frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    enter:
      - command: ui.selectFrame
        args:
          index: 0
        onFailure: skip-action

    complete:
      event: drawing.completed

    fallback: skip-step

  - id: their-turn
    kind: transition

    title: Now watch their side
    body: |
      Ask them to draw something too. This step continues on its own the moment their work reaches you.

    waitFor:
      state: collab.remoteLayerCount
      operator: gte
      value: 1

    timeoutMs: 120000

    fallback:
      type: show-info
      content:
        title: Nothing arrived yet
        body: |
          Their drawing hasn't come through. They may still be getting settled — you can carry on and it will appear whenever they draw.

  - id: who-drew-what
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:layers_panel_toggle} Who drew what"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:layers_panel_toggle} to open the layers panel.

      Each person's work gets its own layer there, labelled with their name. Yours stay yours — you can hide or change your own layers without touching theirs.

    target: layers_panel_toggle
    panel:
      anchor: { target: layers_panel_toggle, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      state: command.isOn
      args:
        command: layers_panel_toggle
      operator: truthy

    fallback: skip-step

  - id: done
    kind: info

    title: That's the whole idea
    body: |
      You draw, they draw, both screens stay in step. Everything you made during this tour is yours to keep.

format: storytilecraft-tour/1

id: handbook.stage1
slug: stage1-frames
version: 1
status: published

title: Stage 1 — Managing frames
description: Create, select, reorder and clone the panels your story is made of.
category: handbook
estimatedMinutes: 6

launch:
  sources: [editor, deep-link]
  autoStart: never
  resume: true
  restart: ask

session:
  content: user
  onEnd: keep

setup:
  - command: ui.setupLocation
    args:
      location: canvas
    onFailure: skip-action

defaults:
  interactionMode: NONE
  advance: manual
  targetPadding: 8
  fallback: skip-step

steps:
  - id: intro
    kind: info

    title: The toolbars
    body: |
      The tools sit along the edges of the screen: frame and drawing tools together along the top, frame-effect tools along the left, playback controls along the bottom, navigation in the bottom-left corner, settings in the top-right.

      Both top toolbars hide extra buttons behind a more button — {icon:cmd:show_more_topmain_tools_toggle} on the top one, {icon:cmd:show_more_topext_tools_toggle} on the left one. This tour walks through the frames your story is built from.

    targets:
      - id: region.topToolbar
        role: primary
        padding: 4
      - id: region.leftToolbar
        role: allowed
        padding: 4
      - id: region.bottomToolbar
        role: allowed
        padding: 4
      - id: nav.frames
        role: allowed
        padding: 4
      - id: region.settings
        role: allowed
        padding: 4
    panel:
      anchor: { target: region.topToolbar, side: auto, margin: 12 }

  - id: add-first-frame
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:add_frame} Create a frame"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:add_frame} on the top toolbar.

      A drawing frame appears on the screen — an empty panel of your story.

    target: add_frame
    panel:
      anchor: { target: add_frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: frame.created
      origin: system

  - id: add-more-frames
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:add_frame} Add two more"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:add_frame} twice more. A story needs somewhere to go.

    target: add_frame
    panel:
      anchor: { target: add_frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      state: frame.count
      operator: gte
      value: 5

  - id: select-frame
    kind: interaction

    title: Choose a frame
    body: |
      Two ways to select a frame:

      - tap the frame itself;
      - tap its numbered circle in the bottom-left corner.

      The selected frame moves to the centre and takes an **orange** outline. The others stay grey.

    targets:
      - id: canvas.frame
        role: primary
        args:
          index: 0
        padding: 6
      - id: nav.frame
        role: allowed
        args:
          index: 0
        padding: 6
    panel:
      anchor: { target: canvas.frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    # [BUG-022, same shape] Repeat must give the reader something left to do. The gate is
    # `frame.selected.index gte 0`, so a frame selected on the first pass keeps satisfying
    # it and Repeat re-opens a step that is already complete. Clearing the selection first
    # makes the exercise genuinely repeatable — and matches stage2-drawing/pick-frame.
    beforeStep:
      - command: ui.deselectFrame

    complete:
      state: frame.selected.index
      operator: gte
      value: 0

  - id: clone-frame
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:clone_selected_frame} Clone a frame"
    body: |
      With a frame selected, tap {icon:cmd:clone_selected_frame} on the top toolbar.

      A duplicate appears beside the original — useful when the next panel is a small change from this one.

    target: clone_selected_frame
    panel:
      anchor: { target: clone_selected_frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: frame.created
      origin: system

  - id: reorder
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:toggle_frames_ordering_tool} Change the order"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_frames_ordering_tool} to unlock reordering. While it is active you can drag frames freely; tap {icon:cmd:toggle_frames_ordering_tool} again to apply the new order, and the story re-forms into a strip.

    target: toggle_frames_ordering_tool
    panel:
      anchor: { target: toggle_frames_ordering_tool, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: toggle_frames_ordering_tool

  - id: strip
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} Line the story up"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} to arrange every frame into a single strip, centred on screen. This is how you get back to a tidy view after moving things around.

    target: frames_to_strip_exposition
    panel:
      anchor: { target: frames_to_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: frames_to_strip_exposition

  - id: deleting
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:delete_selected_frame_content} Deleting"
    body: |
      {icon:cmd:delete_selected_frame_content} on the top toolbar deletes the **selected frame** — the frame itself and everything drawn in it.

      Tap it now. It asks first: the button turns into a warning, and a **second tap confirms**. Tapping anywhere else cancels.

    target: delete_selected_frame_content
    panel:
      anchor: { target: delete_selected_frame_content, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    enter:
      - command: ui.selectFrame
        args:
          index: 0
        onFailure: skip-action

    complete:
      state: frame.count
      operator: lte
      value: 1

  - id: done
    kind: info

    title: Stage one complete
    body: |
      You can create frames, select them, clone them and put them in order.

      Next: drawing in them.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schemas/tour-author.schema.json


format: storytilecraft-tour/1

id: handbook.stage2
slug: stage2-drawing
version: 1
status: published

title: Stage 2 — Drawing
description: Pencil, eraser, line width and colour — and drawing across several frames.
category: handbook
estimatedMinutes: 5

launch:
  sources: [editor, deep-link]
  autoStart: never
  resume: true
  restart: ask

requirements:
  commands: [editor_draw_mode_toggle, editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle]

session:
  content: user
  onEnd: keep

setup:
  - command: ui.setupLocation
    args:
      location: canvas
    onFailure: skip-action

  - command: layer_tile_scale_slider
    onFailure: skip-action

defaults:
  interactionMode: NONE
  advance: manual
  targetPadding: 8
  fallback: skip-step

steps:
  - id: pick-frame
    kind: interaction

    title: Where your drawing will go
    body: |
      Tap a frame to select it — or tap its numbered circle in the bottom-left corner. The one with the **orange** outline is where your drawing goes.

    targets:
      - id: canvas.frame
        role: primary
        args:
          index: 0
        padding: 6
      - id: nav.frame
        role: allowed
        args:
          index: 0
        padding: 6
    panel:
      anchor: { target: canvas.frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    beforeStep:
      - command: ui.deselectFrame
      - command: ui.enableMoveMode

    complete:
      state: frame.selected.index
      operator: gte
      value: 0

  - id: pencil
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} The pencil"
    body: |
      You are already holding it — drawing is the editor's default mode.

      {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} on the top toolbar chooses which SIDE of the canvas you
      draw on, rather than turning drawing on and off. Tap it once to move behind your artwork,
      and again to come back in front.

    beforeStep:
      - command: ui.enableMoveMode

    target: editor_draw_mode_toggle
    panel:
      anchor: { target: editor_draw_mode_toggle, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: editor_draw_mode_toggle

  - id: draw
    kind: interaction

    title: Draw something
    body: |
      Draw the number **1** in the selected frame.

      The speed of your hand sets the thickness of the line — move faster for a thicker stroke.

    target:
      id: canvas.frame
      args:
        index: 0
      padding: 6
    panel:
      anchor: { target: canvas.frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: drawing.completed

  - id: line-width
    kind: interaction

    title: Line width
    body: |
      The slider on the top toolbar, just under the tool icons, sets stroke thickness. Move it, then draw again to feel the difference.

    target: control.lineWidth
    panel:
      anchor: { target: control.lineWidth, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: layer_tile_scale_slider

  - id: colour
    kind: interaction

    title: Change the colour
    body: |
      Pick a colour you like from the strip. Everything you draw from now on uses it.

    target: panel.palette
    panel:
      anchor: { target: panel.palette, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: color.selected

  - id: eraser
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle} The eraser"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle} and rub out part of what you drew. Tap {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} again to go back to drawing.

    beforeStep:
      - command: ui.enableDrawMode

    target: editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle
    panel:
      anchor: { target: editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle

  - id: next-frame
    kind: interaction

    title: Move to the next frame
    body: |
      Tap the circle numbered **2** in the bottom-left corner. The second frame comes to the centre.

      One tap centres a frame; a second tap enlarges it for detailed work.

    targets:
      - id: nav.frame
        role: primary
        args:
          index: 1
        padding: 6
      - id: canvas.frame
        role: allowed
        args:
          index: 1
        padding: 6
    panel:
      anchor: { target: nav.frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      state: frame.selected.index
      operator: gte
      value: 1

  - id: draw-again
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} Draw in it"
    body: |
      Draw the number **2** here. Then do the same in the third frame, and you have a story of three panels.

    target:
      id: canvas.frame
      args:
        index: 1
      padding: 6
    panel:
      anchor: { target: canvas.frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      state: frame.selected.hasContent
      operator: truthy

  - id: done
    kind: info

    title: Stage two complete
    body: |
      You have drawn a story. Step by step it becomes simple, if you give yourself a little time and calmly press the right buttons.

      Next: playing it back.

locales.ua:
title: "Етап 2 — Малювання"
description: "Олівець, гумка, товщина лінії, колір і малювання в кількох кадрах."

steps:
  pick-frame:
    title: "Куди потрапить ваш малюнок"
    body: "Торкніться кадру, щоб обрати його — або його пронумерованого кружечка внизу ліворуч. Той, що з **помаранчевою** рамкою, — саме туди й потрапить малюнок."

    title: "{icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} Олівець"
    body: "Ви вже тримаєте його — малювання ввімкнене за замовчуванням.\n\n{icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} на верхній панелі обирає, з якого БОКУ полотна ви малюєте, а не вмикає й вимикає малювання. Торкніться раз, щоб перейти за свій малюнок, і ще раз, щоб повернутися перед ним."
  draw:
    title: "Намалюйте щось"
    body: "Намалюйте цифру **1** у вибраному кадрі.\n\nШвидкість руху руки визначає товщину лінії: рухайтеся швидше, щоб штрих був товстішим."
  line-width:
    title: "Товщина лінії"
    body: "Повзунок на верхній панелі, одразу під іконками інструментів, задає товщину штриха. Посуньте його й намалюйте ще раз, щоб відчути різницю."
  colour:
    title: "Змініть колір"
    body: "Відкрийте палітру й виберіть колір, який вам подобається. Усе, що ви малюватимете далі, буде цього кольору."
  eraser:
    title: "{icon:cmd:editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle} Гумка"
    body: "Торкніться {icon:cmd:editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle} і зітріть частину намальованого. Торкніться {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} ще раз, щоб повернутися до малювання."
  next-frame:
    title: "Перейдіть до наступного кадру"
    body: "Торкніться кружечка з цифрою **2** внизу ліворуч. Другий кадр переміститься в центр.\n\nОдне торкання центрує кадр, а друге збільшує його для детального малювання."
  draw-again:
    title: "{icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} Намалюйте в ньому"
    body: "Намалюйте тут цифру **2**. Потім зробіть те саме в третьому кадрі — і матимете історію з трьох панелей."
  done:
    title: "Другий етап завершено"
    body: "Ви вже намалювали історію. Крок за кроком усе стає простим, якщо дати собі трохи часу й спокійно натискати потрібні кнопки.\n\nДалі — відтворення історії."

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schemas/tour-author.schema.json


format: storytilecraft-tour/1

id: handbook.stage3
slug: stage3-playing
version: 1
status: published

title: Stage 3 — Playing the story
description: Play, pause, speed, reverse, and stepping frame by frame.
category: handbook
estimatedMinutes: 4

launch:
  sources: [editor, deep-link]
  autoStart: never
  resume: true
  restart: ask

requirements:
  commands: [toggle_play_strip_exposition]

session:
  content: user
  onEnd: keep

setup:
  - command: ui.setupLocation
    args:
      location: canvas
    onFailure: skip-action

defaults:
  interactionMode: NONE
  advance: manual
  targetPadding: 8
  fallback: skip-step

steps:
  - id: where-it-starts
    kind: info

    title: Where playback begins
    body: |
      If a frame has the orange outline, the story plays **from that frame**. To play from the beginning, select frame **1** first.

      With nothing selected, the story plays from the start.

  - id: play
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} Play"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} on the bottom toolbar and watch your story run.

    target: toggle_play_strip_exposition
    panel:
      anchor: { target: toggle_play_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      state: command.isOn
      args:
        command: toggle_play_strip_exposition
      operator: truthy

  - id: pause
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} Pause"
    body: |
      The same button pauses it while it is playing. Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} again.

    beforeStep:
      - command: ui.armForcedPause

    target: toggle_play_strip_exposition
    panel:
      anchor: { target: toggle_play_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      state: command.isOn
      args:
        command: toggle_play_strip_exposition
      operator: falsy

  - id: speed
    kind: interaction

    title: Change the speed
    body: |
      Pick a playback speed: **4×** (fastest), **2×**, **1×**, **0.5×**, **0.25×** (slowest).

      Slower is often better for looking at what you drew.

    target: set_speed_of_play_strip_exposition
    panel:
      anchor: { target: set_speed_of_play_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: set_speed_of_play_strip_exposition

  - id: stop
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:stop_strip_exposition} Stop"
    body: |
      {icon:cmd:stop_strip_exposition} stops playback. Pressing play afterwards starts again from the beginning, rather than resuming.

    target:
      id: stop_strip_exposition
      allowDisabled: true
    panel:
      anchor: { target: stop_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: stop_strip_exposition

  - id: more-tools
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:show_more_player_tools_toggle} The hidden player buttons"
    body: |
      Reverse playback lives behind {icon:cmd:show_more_player_tools_toggle}, to the right of the stop button. Tap it to reveal the extra controls.

    target: show_more_player_tools_toggle
    panel:
      anchor: { target: show_more_player_tools_toggle, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      state: command.isOn
      args:
        command: show_more_player_tools_toggle
      operator: truthy

  - id: reverse
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:reverse_strip_exposition} Play it backwards"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:reverse_strip_exposition}, then play. The story runs in reverse — a different thing to watch than the same story forwards.

    target: reverse_strip_exposition
    panel:
      anchor: { target: reverse_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    enter:
      - command: show_more_player_tools_toggle
        when:
          state: command.isOn
          args:
            command: show_more_player_tools_toggle
          operator: falsy
        onFailure: skip-action

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: reverse_strip_exposition

  - id: step-forward
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:next_action_strip_exposition} Step to the next frame"
    body: |
      {icon:cmd:next_action_strip_exposition} moves the focus one frame on. Keep tapping and it loops around — there is no end to run off.

    target: next_action_strip_exposition
    panel:
      anchor: { target: next_action_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    enter:
      - command: show_more_player_tools_toggle
        when:
          state: command.isOn
          args:
            command: show_more_player_tools_toggle
          operator: falsy
        onFailure: skip-action

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: next_action_strip_exposition

  - id: tidy-up
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} Back to a strip"
    body: |
      After playback the frames may be scattered. {icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} returns them to a strip in the centre of the screen.

    target: frames_to_strip_exposition
    panel:
      anchor: { target: frames_to_strip_exposition, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: frames_to_strip_exposition

  - id: done
    kind: info

    title: Stage three complete
    body: |
      You can not only draw a story now, but control it.

      Next — the most interesting part: doing things to the drawings themselves.

locales.ua:
title: "Етап 3 — Відтворення історії"
description: "Відтворення, пауза, швидкість, зворотний порядок і перехід між кадрами."

    title: "{icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} Пауза"

    title: "{icon:cmd:stop_strip_exposition} Зупиніть"
    body: "{icon:cmd:stop_strip_exposition} зупиняє відтворення. Якщо після цього натиснути відтворення, історія почнеться з початку, а не продовжиться."

    title: "{icon:cmd:show_more_player_tools_toggle} Приховані кнопки плеєра"

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schemas/tour-author.schema.json


format: storytilecraft-tour/1

id: handbook.stage4
slug: stage4-gamifiers
version: 1
status: published

title: Stage 4 — Frame tools and gamifiers
description: Narrative, thermometer, background, and the fire and shatter workspaces.
category: handbook
estimatedMinutes: 8

launch:
  sources: [editor, deep-link]
  autoStart: never
  resume: true
  restart: ask

requirements:
  commands: [toggle_frame_speech_editor, burn_frame]

session:
  content: user
  onEnd: keep

setup:
  - command: ui.setupLocation
    args:
      location: canvas
    onFailure: skip-action

defaults:
  interactionMode: NONE
  advance: manual
  targetPadding: 8
  fallback: skip-step

steps:
  - id: select-first
    kind: interaction

    title: These tools act on one frame
    body: |
      Everything in this stage applies to the **selected** frame — the one with the orange outline. The first one is selected already.

      To aim these tools at a different frame, tap it, or its numbered circle.

    targets:
      - id: canvas.frame
        role: primary
        args:
          index: 0
        padding: 6
      - id: nav.frame
        role: allowed
        args:
          index: 0
        padding: 6
    panel:
      anchor: { target: canvas.frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    enter:
      - command: ui.selectFrame
        args:
          index: 0
        onFailure: skip-action

    complete:
      state: frame.selected.index
      operator: gte
      value: 0

  - id: narrative
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:toggle_frame_speech_editor} Add a narrative"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_frame_speech_editor} on the top toolbar. The frame moves to the centre and a speech bubble opens beside it.

      Type something — «This is number 1» — and press **✓** to apply. The editor also has 🗑️ to clear and **✗** to cancel.

    target: toggle_frame_speech_editor
    panel:
      anchor: { target: toggle_frame_speech_editor, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: toggle_frame_speech_editor

  - id: thermometer
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:toggle_frame_thermometer} Add a thermometer"
    body: |
      Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_frame_thermometer}. A scale from 1 to 10 appears at the left edge — drag its slider to set where this frame sits.

      The same button removes it again.

    target: toggle_frame_thermometer
    panel:
      anchor: { target: toggle_frame_thermometer, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: toggle_frame_thermometer

  - id: background
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:portal_frame_set_aura} Colour the frame"
    body: |
      Choose a colour in the palette, then tap {icon:cmd:portal_frame_set_aura} on the top toolbar. The frame takes that colour as its background.

    target: portal_frame_set_aura
    panel:
      anchor: { target: portal_frame_set_aura, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    complete:
      event: command.executed
      match:
        command: portal_frame_set_aura

  - id: gamifier-panel
    kind: info

    title: "{icon:cmd:toggle_effects_bar} Turning the gamifiers on"
    body: |
      Gamifiers are off until you enable them: **⚙ Settings → TF-CBT → Enable gamification elements**.

      With them on, a joystick icon appears in the bottom-right corner and the effect buttons become available on the top toolbar.

  - id: shatter
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:shatter_frame} Shattering"
    body: |
      Select a frame and tap {icon:cmd:shatter_frame}. The frame moves into its own workspace.

      Tap the drawing anywhere and it shatters like glass. The slider on the left changes how fast, and a restore button brings the image back.

    target: shatter_frame
    panel:
      anchor: { target: shatter_frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    enter:
      - command: ui.setupLocation
        args:
          location: canvas
        onFailure: skip-action

    complete:
      event: gamifier.opened
      origin: system

    fallback:
      type: show-info
      content:
        title: The gamifier controls are not available
        body: |
          These effects only appear once gamification is on: **⚙ Settings → TF-CBT → Enable gamification elements**.

          Turn it on and start this tour again to try shattering, or press Next to carry on without it.

  - id: back-from-shatter
    kind: transition

    title: Come back when you are done
    body: |
      Play with it for as long as you like. Press the return button to come back to the story, and this tour picks up again.

    waitFor:
      state: gamifier.active
      operator: falsy

    waitAfter: gamifier.opened

    timeoutMs: 300000

    fallback:
      type: show-info
      content:
        title: Still in the workspace
        body: |
          No hurry — the tour will wait. If you would rather carry on, press Next.

  - id: fire
    kind: interaction

    title: "{icon:cmd:burn_frame} Fire"
    body: |
      Select a frame and tap {icon:cmd:burn_frame}. Swipe across the drawing and it begins to burn.

      Inside that workspace you can shield part of the image from the flames, add fuel so it catches faster, make the flames bigger with the sliders, and put them out with the extinguisher. A restore button brings the image back at any point.

    target: burn_frame
    panel:
      anchor: { target: burn_frame, side: auto, margin: 12 }

    enter:
      - command: ui.setupLocation
        args:
          location: canvas
        onFailure: skip-action

    complete:
      event: gamifier.opened
      origin: system

    fallback:
      type: show-info
      content:
        title: The gamifier controls are not available
        body: |
          Fire needs gamification switched on: **⚙ Settings → TF-CBT → Enable gamification elements**.

          Turn it on and start this tour again to try it, or press Next to carry on without it.

  - id: back-from-fire
    kind: transition

    title: Come back when you are done
    body: |
      Press the return button when you have finished burning things.

    waitFor:
      state: gamifier.active
      operator: falsy

    waitAfter: gamifier.opened

    timeoutMs: 300000

    fallback:
      type: show-info
      content:
        title: Still in the workspace
        body: |
          Take your time. Press Next when you want to carry on.

  - id: filters
    kind: info

    title: "{icon:cmd:gray_scale_filter_value_slider} Colour and composition"
    body: |
      There is one more workspace, opened from the top toolbar, for changing how a drawing looks rather than destroying it: grayscale, blur, hue rotation, colour filters, and folding the image.

      Folding is worth knowing about: a folded image **stays folded** when you return to the story. Unfold it in the same workspace where you folded it.

  - id: done
    kind: info

    title: Stage four complete
    body: |
      You have worked on individual frames of a drawn story — narrative, temperature, colour, and taking an image apart.

      That is the whole first level of the app.

format: storytilecraft-tour/1

id: handbook.stage5
slug: stage5-saving
version: 1
status: published

title: Stage 5 — Saving and restoring
description: Keep a story as a file, and bring it back.
category: handbook
estimatedMinutes: 2

launch:
  sources: [editor, deep-link]
  autoStart: never
  resume: true
  restart: ask

session:
  content: user
  onEnd: keep

defaults:
  interactionMode: NONE
  advance: manual
  targetPadding: 8

steps:
  - id: why
    kind: info

    title: Your story is a file
    body: |
      A story can be saved to a file and loaded back later — on this device or another one. Nothing is uploaded anywhere: the file is yours.

  - id: save
    kind: info

    title: "{icon:cmd:basic_save_json_file} Saving"
    body: |
      1. Tap the **⚙** gear in the top-right corner.
      2. In **Settings**, go to **Storage** in the left-hand menu.
      3. Tap **Save story to JSON file**.

      A short message confirms the file has been downloaded.

  - id: restore
    kind: info

    title: "{icon:cmd:basic_load_json_file} Restoring"
    body: |
      1. Tap the **⚙** gear again.
      2. **Settings → Storage**.
      3. Tap **Upload story from JSON file** and pick your file.

      The story loads straight into the workspace.

  - id: warning
    kind: info

    title: One thing worth knowing
    body: |
      Loading a story **replaces** what is on screen. If you have unsaved work, save it first.

  - id: done
    kind: info

    title: That is the whole handbook
    body: |
      Frames, drawing, playback, per-frame tools, and saving.

      You have seen the first level of the app end to end. Everything else builds on these.
